AUTHOR: Kandimalla
TITLE: Automated Detection, Classification and Counting of Fish in Fish Passages With Deep Learning
REGION: Optical: Wells Dam fish ladder, Columbia River, Washington, USA (sonar part: Ocqueoc River, Michigan, USA)
SPECIES: Optical: single 'fish' class (videos contain Chinook, Jack Chinook, Sockeye salmon); sonar part: 8 species (carp, lamprey, largemouth bass, pike, smallmouth bass, steelhead, sucker, walleye)
DATA: Public Wells Dam fish-ladder optical video dataset (Xu & Matzner 2018 / PNNL EyeSea), 24,000 frames; public Ocqueoc River DIDSON sonar dataset (McCann et al. 2018) for the sonar part
V_EV: no statement found (only generic Introduction remark about 'luminosity variation, fish camouflage, complex backgrounds, water murkiness'; nothing on the Wells Dam footage)
D_EV: Sec. 2.2.2.1: 'into 19,200 images for training and 4800 images for testing by randomly selecting videos to have no overlap of videos between the train and test sets.'
R_EV: Sec. 2.2.2.1: 'We first split the 24,000 frames of video in the Wells Dam Camera dataset into 19,200 images for training and 4800 images for testing'
C_EV: Table 7: 'the number of false positives (FP), false negatives (FN), ID switches (IDs), fragmentation (FM), and multiple object tracking accuracy (MOTA)'
E_EV: Sec. 4: 'The greatest MOTA attained by Norfair was 66.9% for 20 fps videos, 66.2% for 10 fps videos, and 62.2% for 5 fps videos' (tracking metrics only; no fish counts reported)
ARCH: Optical: YOLOv4 (CSPDarknet53, 608x608, 1 class) + Norfair Kalman-filter tracker (initialization_delay tuned 6-17); sonar: YOLOv3 and Mask-RCNN (ResNet-101 FPN)
METR: Tracking: MOTA, MT/PT/ML, FP, FN, ID switches, fragmentation (CVPR19/CLEAR metrics) at 5/10/20 fps; sonar: mAP and per-class AP at IoU 0.4/0.5, TP/FP counts
NOTE: Mixed sonar + optical paper; coded for the optical (Wells Dam fish ladder) component only, per inclusion flag. Sonar detection/classification results (mAP 0.73 YOLOv3) are out of scope. D: optical train/test split is explicitly by video; D4=Y also supported by the sonar-part statement that frames were labelled 'every few frames' to 'reduce the potential that two nearly identical images will appear in both the training and test sets'. C1=NR: the text only says generically that 'one applies a confidence threshold (typically 0.5)' in the metrics section; no threshold is stated for the trained YOLOv4/Norfair models (verifier may read this as C1=Y, which would make C_ALL=Y). C5: ID switches, FP and fragmentation are quantified per frame rate and initialization delay, and the authors discuss ID switches as an obstacle to accurate counting. E: although the title says 'counting', no fish counts or comparisons with manual counts are reported — only MOTA-type tracking metrics — so E1=없음. PRE: the text says YOLOv4/YOLOv3 weights were 'pre-trained on the ImageNet dataset' (though it then mentions 80 classes, suggesting COCO); coded as stated. NIMG=24,000 optical frames (13,405 with fish). Both datasets are public third-party datasets (DSHR=공개); no code release.
